title: Commitment Mosaic: micro-bands, staged SLAs, and surge-credit simulations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: design and validate a multi-dimensional commitment product ('Commitment Mosaic') that combines small-duration micro-bands, staged SLA tiers, and surge-credit mechanics to reduce churn from unpredictable throughput patterns while preserving unit economics. This ticket covers modeling, customer segmentation, contract language draft, legal/security questionnaire inputs, and a gated experiment with 5 pilot customers. Deliverables: pricing model, SLA ladder definitions, surge-credit allocation rules, rollback criteria, PRD, and legal Q&A for Security/Privacy team. Links: PRD draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Commitment+Mosaic+PRD, experiment dashboard prototype https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/commitment-mosaic, contract language sketch https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/commitment-mosaic-contracts
acceptance_criteria: Simulated P&L model showing >=5% average margin improvement vs baseline for at least 3 of 5 workload archetypes (batch-heavy, chat-low-latency, embedding-bursty)
Clear SLA tier definitions (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with target p50/p95 latency bands, burst allowance, and explicit preemption/soft-fail behavior
Surge-credit algorithm documented with deterministic refund/backfill rules and example calculations for 3 real customer traces
Legal and Security questionnaire answers produced for top 20 enterprise control questions (SSO/KMS/PII handling/regions), with sign-off from Security
Experiment plan and billing/rate-limiting guardrails implemented in console for pilot customers and rollback/cancel paths defined
notes: 2026-02-11: Kickoff with PM, Finance, Runtime, and Legal. Agreed scope includes micro-bands (<=7d commitments) + staged SLA ladder; Marketing to coordinate naming taxonomy.
2026-02-18: Finance provided baseline unit economics model (sheet link in PRD). Initial observation: burst-heavy customers benefit from surge-credits but risk margin pressure if not rate-limited.
2026-02-24: Runtime eng (ENG-19412) requested clarifications: required telemetry to support per-customer surge allocation and ability to enforce soft-preemption on low-tier pools.

2026-03-01: Legal flagged four SSQ items required for enterprise pilots (KMS integration scope, audit log retention, data residency language, subcontractor list). Added as hard blockers until Security review completes.

2026-03-05: Trade-offs discussion: aggressive surge credits improve sales-conversion but increase cost variance and operational complexity. Decision: phase 1 will limit surge credits to 20% of committed capacity per calendar month and enforce a progressive degradation policy rather than hard preemption.

2026-03-09: Experiment design finalised. Pilot cohort to include 5 customers across small/medium/large segments. Success signals defined: conversion to 12-month commits, <2% invocation of manual refunds, and stable 95th percentile latency within SLA 95% of time.

2026-03-10: Security review scheduled. Assigned Security reviewer: Elena Ruiz. Added to Q2 compliance intake for KMS attestation. Next step: complete SSQ answers and legal contract clause drafts by 2026-03-24.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (Modeling): run Monte Carlo simulations on historical traces (2w) - Finance + Data Science
Phase 1 (Contract & Controls): draft SLA ladder + surge-credit terms; legal & security checklist (3w)
Phase 2 (Runtime): telemetry + enforcement APIs + console bill presentation for pilots (4w)
Phase 3 (Pilot): onboard 5 customers, monitor for 8 weeks, collect conversion and latency metrics (8w)
Phase 4 (Evaluation & Scale): iterate pricing, document playbook, prepare GA runbook (3w)
risks: Revenue leakage from overly-generous surge credits if traffic correlations are misestimated
Operational load on SRE during pilot if soft-preemption semantics cause customer visible errors
Enterprise legal negotiations may require longer lead time for KMS/HSM attestations
Complexity in UI/contract may confuse sales; need standardized one-page cheat-sheet for AE teams
